reviews.frank_statement: A validated CognitiveFrame should be the causal consistency boundary for one workspace/model turn, using a basis root plus scoped revision witnesses and escalation for unknown closure.
ancestry_families: CC7/CC8 scoped freshness and OTCC returned through FRANK C4
reviews.counterhypothesis: One atomic global snapshot/root is sufficient, or independent latest reads are harmless because components are semantically decoupled.
reviews.falsifier: On representative live FRANK/ClayGraph traces, independent latest reads never create incompatible model-visible combinations, or one atomic root completely determines graph, activation, frame and projection compatibility without extra witnesses.
independent_checks: CC9 new local multi-epoch counterexample: 8.9555% constructed mixed tuples; exact required tuple accepted 0 mixed.
CC9 independent Judge0 replication: 8.736% constructed mixed tuples; 0 mixed passed tuple validation.
Distributed causal/snapshot literature independently requires explicit causal metadata or snapshot handles when multiple state locations must be observed consistently.
adversarial_checks: Changed an unrelated telemetry epoch while required frame/graph/activation witnesses remained valid; CC-RC1.4 reference allowed the operation, showing the refined rule is operation-specific rather than universal tuple equality.
Made activation epoch stale while frame/graph matched; reference rejected.
reviews.reason: The consistency-boundary idea survives, but ClayCode should represent a typed operation-specific Causal Basis vector/compatibility certificate rather than treating CognitiveFrame or a single state root as the universal basis. ClayGraph graph/activation epochs are first-class basis dimensions when an operation actually depends on them.

reviews.frank_statement: Model/Qwen/Needle output is proposal, not authority; external capability gateway/K0 remains the sole authority for external effects.
ancestry_families: CC-RC1.1/CC8 authority boundary returned through FRANK
reviews.counterhypothesis: A sufficiently constrained small model can safely interpret compact capability/freshness semantics and authorize effects directly.
reviews.falsifier: A preregistered target Qwen3-4B authority corpus plus adversarial/OOD cases yields zero unsafe ACCEPTs and equivalent policy enforcement to the deterministic gateway under all tested dynamic/alias/epoch cases.
independent_checks: CC9 new Groq 8B raw semantic arm achieved only 1/10 exact classifications, while deterministic precompilation + model relay achieved 10/10.

Current Koka documentation independently demonstrates static tracking/composition of effects; WebAssembly component/resource boundaries independently separate host-provided external functionality from component computation.
2026 Proof-Carrying Agent Actions proposes runtime-neutral action certificates and external governance checkpoints rather than model self-authorization.
adversarial_checks: Raw 8B reader collapsed many distinct failure reasons into EFFECT, demonstrating that compact/small-model semantic reading can fail systematically rather than randomly.
CC9 dynamic-dispatch and alias tests show that even a correct textual proposal can omit hidden authority-relevant resource identities.
reviews.reason: Independent current proxy/model and systems evidence support keeping authority outside the generative reader. This preserves the original evidence status: architectural/safety support, not production-security proof.

reviews.frank_statement: Semantic workspace state and the model-facing Word/text projection are distinct; projection should be deterministic/versioned rather than defining canonical truth.
ancestry_families: CC6/CC8 semantic-IR/projection separation returned through FRANK
reviews.counterhypothesis: A single compact wire/text surface can serve simultaneously as canonical semantic identity and optimal small-model reader representation.
reviews.falsifier: Target-model and roundtrip tests show one surface preserves semantic identity across schema/wire changes, achieves equal/better reader accuracy/cost, and requires no independent projection integrity receipt.
independent_checks: CC9 new 100k projection mutation reference test separated semantic corruption detection from wire-only mutation detection with 100% detection in the constructed checker.
CC9 new Groq raw-vs-certified projection test: 1/10 vs 10/10 exact and 327 vs 152 prompt tokens.
Contemporaneous Clay G9 raw-vs-compiled proxy: 5/10 vs 9/10 exact and 487 vs 324 prompt tokens; same provider/worker family, therefore supporting but not independent replication.
adversarial_checks: Changed only wire whitespace: semantic hash stayed stable while projection hash changed.
Changed projection semantics/value: semantic identity check changed, preventing a transport-level success from being mistaken for semantic reconstruction.
reviews.reason: Separation is retained and strengthened: model-facing projections need a projection-schema/semantic receipt, and high-stakes decisions should be precompiled by the deterministic kernel rather than re-derived from compact text by the model.

reviews.frank_statement: The current candidate uses six workspace channels and a default ignition threshold of 0.55.
reviews.counterhypothesis: Channel cardinality and ignition threshold are runtime/configuration parameters that may vary by architecture/version and should not be ClayCode language constants.
reviews.falsifier: Independent mechanistic/live evidence establishes exactly six channels and 0.55 as invariant semantic necessities across supported FRANK architectures rather than current configuration values.
adversarial_checks: Represented the same workspace schema with alternate channel counts/threshold values; no ClayCode core primitive or authority rule requires six or 0.55.
reviews.reason: ClayCode must represent these values and version them, but current evidence does not justify baking them into language semantics.
